thread.title: Indonesia Bourse Likely To Give Up Support At 6,000 Points

author: RTTNews
title: Indonesia Bourse Likely To Give Up Support At 6,000 Points
text:
(RTTNews) - Ahead of Tuesday's holiday, the Indonesia stock market had snapped the four-day winning streak in which it had advanced more than 235 points or 4 percent in that span. The Jakarta Composite Index now rests just above the 6,005-point plateau and it may extend its losses on Wednesday.
The global forecast for the Asian markets is weak thanks to disappointing earnings news, plummeting crude oil prices and trade concerns. The European and U.S. markets were down and the Asian bourses figure to follow that lead.
The JCI finished slightly lower on Monday as losses from the resource stocks were mitigated by support from the financial shares.
For the day, the index eased 7.05 points or 0.12 percent to finish at 6,005.30 after trading between 5,974.13 and 6,036.99.
Among the actives, Bukit Darmo Property climbed 1.67 percent, while Voksel Electric jumped 1.60 percent, Lotte Chemical added 0.60 percent, Bank Pan Indonesia spiked 4.50 percent, SLJ Global advanced 1.06 percent, Jasa Marga perked 0.50 percent, XL Axiata shed 0.45 percent, Bank Danamon Indonesia collected 0.34 percent, Bank Central Asia gathered 1.11 percent, Bank Mandiri was up 0.34 percent, Bank Negara Indonesia accelerated 1.20 percent, Bank Rakyat Indonesia gained 0.86 percent, Indosat lost 0.92 percent, Bumi Resources plummeted 4.09 percent, Vale Indonesia plunged 4.27 percent, Aneka Tambang dropped 0.74 percent, Indocement fell 1.88 percent, Semen Indonesia picked up 0.91 percent, United Tractors gave away 1.15 percent and Bank MNC Internasional and Indofood were unchanged.
The lead from Wall Street is brutal as stocks showed another significant move to the downside on Tuesday, sending the tech-heavy NASDAQ to its lowest closing level in over seven months.
The Dow plunged 551.80 points or 2.21 percent to 24,465.64, while the NASDAQ shed 119.65 points or 1.70 percent to 6,908.82 and the S&P 500 fell 48.84 points or 1.82 percent to 2,641.89.
The continued weakness on Wall Street reflected disappointing earnings news from companies such as Target (TGT), Kohl's (KSS) and Victoria's Secret parent L Brands (LB). A continued decline by Apple (AAPL) also weighed on the markets.
On the U.S. economic front, a report from the Commerce Department showed housing starts rebounded in October, although the report also showed a decrease in building permits.
Oil prices plunged sharply on Tuesday as rising concerns about the global economic outlook outweighed optimism of production cuts by OPEC and allies. Crude oil futures for January ended down $3.77 or 6.6 percent at $53.43 a barrel, the lowest settlement price in 13 months.
